issues: Integrity is fine. The diff only lowers the probabilities of two perturbation moves in the search loop: swapping the largest circle goes from 0.2 to 0.1, and re-seeding the smallest circle goes from the 0.1 band to 0.1–0.2. It doesn't touch files or the network, contains no pasted coordinates, and doesn't change validation.

The candidate's adjusted value is -0.0, which means a sum of radii of 0. That almost certainly means the run crashed or returned an invalid packing, which the harness scores as 0. It is not a real result. The tiny diff doesn't obviously explain a crash. It could be a stochastic timeout or an overlap that wasn't shrunk away. Either way it's a failed run, not a manipulation, so the reject is right. It doesn't call for a veto.

The incumbent has only one run, so z can't be computed from a sample standard deviation. The reported z matches a difference of about 2.636 divided by a floor standard deviation of about 1.414e-6 (sqrt(2)*1e-6). That gives about -1.864e6, which is consistent with the harness number to within rounding of the incumbent mean. The size of z means nothing here beyond showing the candidate is far worse.
If the slot budget allows, it may be worth one replicate to check whether the crash is deterministic for this seed. It is not required.

recomputed.note: approx; (-0.0 - (-2.636)) / ~1.414e-6 floor sd, sign per harness convention (negative = worse)
